data.label: Code Flash
data.description: Stores ABS control firmware and safety-critical braking algorithms.

data.label: Data Flash
data.description: Stores calibration parameters, variant coding, and NVM configuration for the ABS ECU.

data.label: Keys
data.description: Cryptographic keys for secure boot, ECU authentication, and UDS seed-key access.

data.label: Certificates
data.description: X.509 certificates used for secure ECU authentication and OTA update validation.

data.label: Debug Port
data.description: JTAG/SWD debug interface for firmware development and diagnostic access. Must be locked in production.

data.label: Wheel Speed Sensors
data.description: Four hall-effect / magnetoresistive sensors (FL, FR, RL, RR) delivering wheel rotation data to the ABS ECU via PWM signal lines.

data.label: Hydraulic Control Unit
data.description: Electro-hydraulic actuator block (solenoid valves + pump motor) that modulates brake pressure per MCU commands.

data.label: CAN Transceiver
data.description: Physical-layer CAN-FD transceiver bridging the MCU CAN controller to the in-vehicle CAN bus.

data.label: OBD-II Interface
data.description: Standardized diagnostic connector exposing UDS services (0x22 ReadDataByIdentifier, 0x27 SecurityAccess, 0x34/0x36 firmware update). Doorway for authorised and adversarial diagnostic sessions.

data.label: Vehicle CAN Bus
data.description: In-vehicle CAN/CAN-FD network shared with ECM, ESP/ESC, BCM, and Gateway. Carries ABS status messages and receives vehicle speed / torque requests.

data.label: ECM (Engine Control Module)
data.description: External node — provides vehicle speed and engine torque signals to ABS over CAN; receives ABS active flag to manage traction.

data.label: Brake Pressure Data
data.description: Real-time hydraulic pressure values per wheel channel computed by the ABS control algorithm.

data.label: Diagnostic Data
data.description: DTC (Diagnostic Trouble Codes) and freeze-frame snapshots stored in NVM; read via OBD-II UDS services.

Derivations.name: CWE-494: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
Derivations.loss: Unauthorized firmware modification via OTA or diagnostic service
Derivations.damageScene: An attacker delivers a tampered firmware image to the ABS ECU through an unsecured OTA channel or an unlocked UDS 0x34/0x36 session. The modified firmware disables the wheel lock prevention logic, causing the ABS to fail silently and creating a life-threatening loss-of-braking condition.

Derivations.name: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
Derivations.loss: Compromise of ECU authentication and seed-key mechanism
Derivations.damageScene: Reverse-engineering of the ABS ECU binary reveals a hard-coded seed-key algorithm. An attacker gains full UDS SecurityAccess (0x27), enabling arbitrary memory read/write and firmware reprogramming without valid workshop credentials.

Derivations.name: CAPEC-390: Bypassing Intermediate Forms — Wheel Speed Signal Injection
Derivations.loss: Injection of spoofed wheel speed signals causing inappropriate ABS activation
Derivations.damageScene: An attacker with physical or CAN access injects falsified PWM wheel-speed signals. The ABS MCU misinterprets normal braking as wheel lock and activates pulse modulation, dramatically extending stopping distance and increasing accident risk.

Derivations.name: ATM Technique: CAN Bus Message Injection
Derivations.loss: Injection of spoofed ABS status CAN frames affecting adjacent ECUs
Derivations.damageScene: An adversary connected to the in-vehicle CAN bus transmits fabricated ABS_Active and WheelSpeed CAN frames. The ECM and ESC receive false data, alter torque distribution and stability control, potentially inducing a spin or loss of vehicle stability.

Derivations.name: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Auth Attempts — OBD-II UDS Brute Force
Derivations.loss: Brute-force of UDS SecurityAccess seed-key to gain privileged diagnostic session
Derivations.damageScene: An attacker connects a rogue diagnostic tool to the OBD-II port and performs automated seed-key brute-forcing. After unlocking level 2 security, the attacker reprograms the ABS ECU or corrupts its NVM calibration, degrading braking performance.

Derivations.name: CWE-276: Incorrect Default Permissions on Calibration Data
Derivations.loss: Tampering of ABS calibration parameters degrading stopping distance
Derivations.damageScene: An attacker who obtains UDS programming access overwrites ABS threshold calibration values (slip ratio limits, pressure ramp rates) stored in Data Flash. The modified parameters cause the ABS system to intervene too early or too late, increasing stopping distance beyond ISO 21434 safety targets.

Derivations.name: MITRE ICS T0843: Program Download via Physical JTAG Access
Derivations.loss: Full ECU compromise through unlocked JTAG debug port in production hardware
Derivations.damageScene: A production ABS ECU is found with the JTAG/SWD interface active and unprotected. An attacker extracts the full flash image, patches the binary to disable ABS logic, and re-flashes the modified image indistinguishable from legitimate firmware.

Derivations.name: ATM Technique: Manipulate Control Logic — HCU Actuator Command Injection
Derivations.loss: Denial of braking or asymmetric braking through actuator command injection
Derivations.damageScene: An attacker who has compromised the ABS MCU firmware sends erroneous solenoid valve commands to the HCU. This causes asymmetric brake pressure modulation, locking one wheel while releasing another, resulting in severe vehicle yaw and potential rollover at highway speed.

Derivations.name: CWE-20: Improper Input Validation — Spoofed Sensor Computation Output
Derivations.loss: Falsified brake pressure data corrupting ABS control loop decisions
Derivations.damageScene: Tampered computation inputs cause the ABS algorithm to operate on falsified pressure values. The control loop oscillates between excessive modulation and no modulation, creating brake fade and increasing stopping distance by up to 40%.

Derivations.name: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs — DTC Suppression
Derivations.loss: Suppression or falsification of ABS DTCs concealing safety-critical faults
Derivations.damageScene: An attacker uses an authorised-looking diagnostic tool to clear or overwrite DTC entries after inducing ABS faults. Technicians performing pre-delivery inspections see a clean fault memory and the compromised vehicle is released to the customer.

Details.Name: ABS Firmware Tampering via OTA / UDS
Details.Description: Exploitation of CWE-494 to deliver unsigned/tampered ABS firmware. Disables wheel-lock prevention logic and creates a silent safety-critical failure. Rated Catastrophic for Safety Impact.

Details.name: ABS Firmware Tampering via OTA / UDS
Details.description: Attacker injects unsigned firmware image through OTA or UDS 0x34/0x36. Disables wheel-lock prevention; CAL 3 — special tools and insider knowledge required.

Details.name: Cryptographic Key Extraction via Binary RE
Details.description: Hard-coded seed (CWE-321) reverse-engineered from ECU binary dump. Grants full UDS SecurityAccess level 2, enabling programming session without valid credentials.

Details.name: Wheel Speed Signal Injection (PWM Spoofing)
Details.description: Falsified PWM signals on sensor lines trigger inappropriate ABS activation during normal braking. Requires physical or CAN bus proximity — CAL 2.

Details.name: CAN Bus ABS Frame Injection
Details.description: Fabricated ABS_Active and WheelSpeed CAN frames sent to ECM/ESC. No authentication on CAN — any node on bus can spoof. CAL 2.

Details.name: OBD-II Seed-Key Brute Force Attack
Details.description: Automated UDS 0x27 SecurityAccess brute-force using a 16-bit seed space. Physical OBD-II access required; lockout delay bypass via power cycling — CAL 2.

Details.name: Calibration Tampering via UDS WriteDataByIdentifier
Details.description: Attacker with programming-session access writes malicious calibration records to Data Flash, altering slip-ratio limits. Safety Impact: Major — CAL 3.

Details.name: JTAG Physical Attack — Full Flash Extraction
Details.description: Production ECU with JTAG/SWD unlocked allows full firmware extraction and patch-reflash. One-device attack; requires hardware removal — CAL 2.

scenes.Name: Secure Boot with Cryptographic Firmware Verification
scenes.Description: The ABS ECU shall verify the integrity and authenticity of all firmware images before execution using RSA-2048 or ECDSA-P256 digital signatures stored in an on-chip HSM.

scenes.Name: HSM-Protected Cryptographic Key Storage
scenes.Description: All UDS seed-key material and secure boot keys shall be stored in a dedicated Hardware Security Module (SHE/EVITA Medium) and never exposed to the main CPU RAM in plaintext.

scenes.Name: UDS SecurityAccess Brute-Force Lockout
scenes.Description: The ABS ECU shall enforce exponential backoff and a maximum of 5 failed SecurityAccess (0x27) attempts per key-cycling cycle before locking the programming session for 24 hours.

scenes.Name: CAN Message Authentication (MAC) for Safety-Critical Frames
scenes.Description: All ABS_Active and WheelSpeed CAN frames shall be authenticated using a 32-bit AUTOSAR SecOC MAC. Unauthenticated frames shall be discarded and logged as DTCs.

scenes.Name: Disable JTAG/SWD Debug Interface in Production
scenes.Description: All JTAG and SWD debug interfaces shall be permanently disabled via OTP fuse programming prior to vehicle shipment. Production builds shall enforce this via build-time security policy.

scenes.Name: OTA Update Package Integrity and Anti-Rollback
scenes.Description: OTA update packages shall include a cryptographic hash (SHA-256) and ECDSA signature. The OTA client shall enforce monotonic version counters to prevent rollback attacks.

scenes.Name: Wheel Speed Input Plausibility Checking
scenes.Description: The ABS MCU shall cross-validate all four wheel-speed sensor inputs for physical plausibility (max delta, sensor correlation). Implausible values trigger a safe fallback and DTC C0035.

scenes.Name: Data Flash Write Protection via Hardware Permissions
scenes.Description: ABS calibration parameters in Data Flash shall be protected by hardware write-enable pins and software access tokens. Writes shall only be permitted within a secured programming session with level 3 access.

scenes.Name: [CS-ABS-R1] Implement RSA-2048 Secure Boot Signature Verification
scenes.Description: Integrate a ROM-based secure boot loader verifying firmware SHA-256 hash signed with RSA-2048 before transferring execution. Failure halts the ECU and asserts fail-safe braking.

scenes.Name: [CS-ABS-R2] Store Keys in SHE/EVITA HSM — No Plaintext CPU Exposure
scenes.Description: Provision symmetric keys exclusively through the SHE CMD_LOAD_KEY protocol. The application MCU shall never have direct register access to key material.

scenes.Name: [CS-ABS-R3] Enforce Session Lockout After 5 Failed UDS 0x27 Attempts
scenes.Description: Implement NRC 0x37 (requiredTimeDelayNotExpired) with a 24-hour lockout counter persisted in NVM. Counter shall only reset via a signed unlock token sent from the OEM factory tool.

scenes.Name: [CS-ABS-R4] Apply AUTOSAR SecOC MAC to CAN IDs 0x1A0 and 0x1A8
scenes.Description: Configure SecOC to append a 32-bit Poly1305 MAC to ABS_Active (0x1A0) and WheelSpeed (0x1A8) frames. CRC failures logged as DTC U0001 and message discarded.

scenes.Name: [CS-ABS-R5] OTP-Fuse JTAG Disable in Production Build Process
scenes.Description: Add a manufacturing test step that programs JTAG_EN OTP fuse to 0 before EOL programming. Production firmware build pipeline shall fail-safe if fuse state is not verified.

scenes.Name: [CS-ABS-R6] Wheel Speed Cross-Validation with Max-Delta Threshold
scenes.Description: Compare wheel acceleration between adjacent sensors. Delta exceeding 15 g over 10 ms from a previous stable reading shall disable ABS assist and log DTC C0040.

Details.label: [TSD001] ABS Firmware Tampering via OTA/UDS — Reduce: Implement Secure Boot + OTA ECDSA Signing
[TSD002] Hard-coded Key Compromise — Reduce: Migrate to HSM-based SHE key storage
[TSD003] Wheel Speed Spoofing — Reduce: Enable plausibility cross-validation, DTC C0035
[TSD004] CAN Bus ABS Frame Injection — Reduce: Enforce SecOC MAC on 0x1A0 / 0x1A8
[TSD005] OBD-II Seed-Key Brute Force — Reduce: Lockout after 5 attempts, NVM-persisted counter
[TSD006] Data Flash Calibration Tampering — Reduce: Hardware write-protect + level-3 UDS session requirement
[TSD007] JTAG Physical Attack — Reduce: OTP-fuse JTAG disable in production build step
[TSD008] HCU Actuator Injection — Retain (residual): Monitor via OBD watchdog + firmware integrity check
[TSD009] Brake Pressure Data Integrity — Reduce: Plausibility checks on computed pressure; fallback to raw sensor
[TSD010] DTC Suppression — Reduce: Hash DTC log with HMAC; verify on read; require auth for clear
